1: # Synth for Stata
2: 
3: Stata implementation of the **synthetic control method** for causal
4: inference in comparative case studies, by Alberto Abadie, Alexis
5: Diamond, and Jens Hainmueller.
6: 
7: The method is described in:
8: 
9: > Abadie, A., Diamond, A., & Hainmueller, J. (2010). "Synthetic Control Methods for Comparative Case Studies: Estimating the Effect of California's Tobacco Control Program." *Journal of the American Statistical Association*, 105(490), 493–505.
10: >
11: > Abadie, A., Diamond, A., & Hainmueller, J. (2011). "Synth: An R Package for Synthetic Control Methods in Comparative Case Studies." *Journal of Statistical Software*, 42(13), 1–17.
12: >
13: > Abadie, A., Diamond, A., & Hainmueller, J. (2014). "Comparative Politics and the Synthetic Control Method." *American Journal of Political Science*, 59(2), 495–510.
14: 
15: ## Installation
16: 
17: From within Stata:
18: 
19: ```
20: ssc install synth, all replace
21: ```
22: 
23: Or net-install the development version directly from this repo:
24: 
25: ```stata
26: net install synth, from(https://raw.githubusercontent.com/j-hai/synth-stata/main/s/) replace
27: ```
28: 
29: When net-installing directly from GitHub, Stata installs the command,
30: help, plugin, and Mata files, but not the bundled example datasets.
31: To download `smoking.dta` and `germany.dta` into your current working
32: directory, run:
33: 
34: ```stata
35: net get synth, from(https://raw.githubusercontent.com/j-hai/synth-stata/main/s/)
36: ```
37: 
38: ## Quick start
39: 
40: `smoking.dta` and `germany.dta` are not bundled with Stata; pull them
41: into your current working directory first via `net get` (see
42: Installation above) or download them directly from this repo.
43: 
44: ```stata
45: use smoking, clear
46: tsset state year
47: 
48: synth cigsale beer(1984(1)1988) lnincome retprice age15to24 ///
49:               cigsale(1988) cigsale(1980) cigsale(1975), ///
50:               trunit(3) trperiod(1989) figure
51: ```
52: 
53: The `figure` option draws the treated vs. synthetic-control trajectory.
54: After running `synth`, the standard returns are available:
55: 
56: * `e(RMSPE)` — root mean squared prediction error over the
57:   pre-intervention period
58: * `e(V_matrix)` — diagonal weights on predictors
59: * `e(W_weights)` — control-unit weights with names and ID numbers
60: * `e(X_balance)` — predictor balance: treated vs. synthetic
61: * `e(Y_treated)`, `e(Y_synthetic)` — outcome trajectories
62: 
63: ## What's new in 0.0.8
64: 
65: * **Apple Silicon support.** Universal `synthopt.mac` binary now
66:   includes an arm64 slice; Stata 17+ on M-series Macs running natively
67:   no longer fails with `Could not load plugin: synthopt.plugin`.
68: * C source in `plugin-src/` now compiles cleanly on macOS, Linux, and
69:   Windows without manual edits (was Microsoft-specific before).
70: * Bumped `version` declaration from 9.2 to 13.0; numerous typo fixes
71:   in comments and error messages.
72: 
73: See [`NEWS.md`](NEWS.md) for the full change log.
74: 
75: ## Repository layout
76: 
77: The repo mirrors SSC's letter-directory layout: `net install` delivers
78: the runnable package files, while `net get` downloads the bundled
79: example datasets.
80: 
81: ```
82: s/                   # primary install dir (matches SSC's bocode/s/)
83:   synth.pkg          # SSC package descriptor
84:   synth.ado          # the user-facing command
85:   synth_ll.ado       # loss-function helper (used in nested mode)
86:   synth.sthlp        # in-Stata help text
87:   stata.toc          # SSC TOC
88:   smoking.dta        # canonical example dataset
89:   synthopt.mac       # macOS plugin (universal: arm64 + x86_64)
90:   synthopt.linux32   # Linux 32-bit plugin
91:   synthopt.linux64   # Linux 64-bit plugin
92:   synthopt.win32     # Windows 32-bit plugin
93:   synthopt.win64     # Windows 64-bit plugin
94:   synthopt.plugin    # platform-active plugin (set by installer)
95: 
96: g/
97:   germany.dta        # additional example dataset
98: 
99: l/
100:   lsynth_mata_subr.mlib  # compiled Mata routines
101: 
102: plugin-src/          # C source for the optimizer plugin
103:   synthopt.c, pr_loqo.{c,h}, stplugin.{c,h}
104: 
105: dev/                 # development tooling — not shipped
106:   01_capture_baseline.do   # records the 0.0-7 reference output
107:   02_regression_check.do   # re-runs and diffs against baseline
108:   baseline_0.0-7.txt       # frozen reference (RMSPE, V, W, X)
109: ```
110: 
111: ## Building the plugin from source
112: 
113: ```sh
114: cd plugin-src
115: 
116: # macOS (universal arm64 + x86_64)
117: cc -arch arm64 -arch x86_64 -bundle -fPIC -DSYSTEM=APPLEMAC -O2 \
118:    -o ../synthopt.mac stplugin.c synthopt.c pr_loqo.c
119: 
120: # Linux x86_64
121: cc -shared -fPIC -DSYSTEM=OPUNIX -O2 \
122:    -o ../synthopt.linux64 stplugin.c synthopt.c pr_loqo.c
123: ```
124: 
125: Windows builds use the original Visual Studio solution under the
126: authoritative source tree (not in this repo).

28: {cmd:synth} implements the synthetic control method for causal inference in comparative case studies. {cmd:synth}
29: estimates the effect of an intervention of interest by comparing the evolution of an aggregate
30: outcome {it:depvar} for a unit affected by the intervention 
31: to the
32: evolution of the same aggregate outcome for a synthetic control group. {cmd:synth}
33: constructs this synthetic control group by searching for a weighted combination
34:  of control units chosen to approximate the unit affected by the intervention 
35: in terms of the outcome predictors.
36: The evolution of the outcome for the resulting synthetic control group is an estimate of 
37: the counterfactual of what would have been observed for the
38: affected unit in the absence of the intervention. {cmd:synth} can also be used to 
39: conduct a variety of placebo and permutation tests that produce informative inference regardless of the number of available comparison units and the
40: number of available time-periods. See Abadie and Gardeazabal (2003) and Abadie, Diamond, and Hainmueller (2010, 2014) for details.
41: 
42: {title:Required Settings}
43: 
44: {p 4 8 2}
45: {marker predoptions}
46: {cmd: depvar} the outcome variable.
47: 
48: {p 4 8 2}
49: {cmd: predictorvars} the list of predictor variables. By default, 
50: all predictor variables are averaged over the entire pre-intervention period, which
51: ranges from the earliest time period available in the panel time variable specified in {cmd: tsset} {it:timevar} to
52: the period immediately prior to the intervention specified in {cmd: trperiod}. Missing values 
53: are ignored in the averages.{p_end} 
54: {p 8 8 2}

107: {cmd: counit}({it:numlist}) a list of unit numbers for the control 
108: units as given in the panel id variable specified in {cmd: tsset} {it:panelvar}; see {help tsset}. {cmd: counit()}
109: should be specified as a list of integer numbers (see {help numlist}) and contain at least two control units.
110: The list of control units specified constitute what is called the `donor pool', the 
111: set of potential control units out of which the synthetic control unit is constructed. 
112: Notice that {cmd: counit} is optional, if no {cmd: counit} is specified, the donor pool defaults to all units available in
113: the panel id variable specified in {cmd: tsset}, excluding the unit affected by the intervention
114: specified in {cmd: trunit}.
115: 
116: {p 4 8 2}
117: {cmd: xperiod}({it:numlist}) a list of time periods over which the predictor variables
118:  specified in {help synth##predoptions:{it:predictorvars}}
119: are averaged. The list of time periods refers to the panel time variable specified in {cmd: tsset} {it:timevar}. 
120: For example, if the specified panel time variable is given in years, {cmd: xperiod}(1980(1)1988) 
121: indicates that the predictor variables are averaged over all years from 1980, 1981,...,1988. See {help numlist} on how to 
122: specify lists of numbers.{p_end} 
123: {p 8 8 2}
124: If no {cmd: xperiod} is specified, {cmd: xperiod} defaults to the entire pre-intervention period, which by default
125: ranges from the earliest time period available in the panel time variable to the 
126: period immediately prior to the intervention. Notice that the
127: period of the intervention itself is excluded from the average and missing entries are ignored. 
128: Also notice that variable-specific time periods always take precedence over {cmd: xperiod}.
129: Usually, {cmd: xperiod} is specified to contain a number of pre-intervention periods, although post-intervention 
130: time periods could be included if the predictors are not affected by the intervention.{p_end}
131: 
132: {p 4 8 2}
133: {cmd: mspeperiod}({it:numlist}) a list of pre-intervention time periods over which the mean squared prediction error (MSPE) 
134: should be minimized. The list of time periods refers to the panel time variable specified in {cmd: tsset} {it:timevar};
135:  see {help tsset}. The MSPE refers to the squared deviations between the outcome for the treated unit
136:  and the synthetic control unit summed over all pre-intervention periods specified in {it:mspeperiod(numlist)}. See {help numlist} on how to specify lists of numbers.
137: {p_end}
138: {p 8 8 2}
139: If no {cmd: mspeperiod()} is specified, {cmd: mspeperiod()} defaults to the entire
140:  pre-intervention period ranging from the earliest time period available in the panel time variable to
141: the period immediately prior to the intervention. Notice that the
142: period of the intervention itself is excluded from {cmd: mspeperiod()}.
143: Usually, the 
144: {cmd: mspeperiod()} is specified to cover the whole pre-treatment period up to the time of the intervention, 
145: but other choices are 
146: possible.{p_end}
147: 
148: 
149: {p 4 8 2}
150: {cmd: resultsperiod}({it:numlist}) a list of time periods over which the results of {cmd: synth}

157: {cmd:nested} by default {cmd: synth} uses a data-driven regression based
158: method to obtain the variable weights contained in the V-matrix. This method 
159: relies on a constrained quadratic programming routine, that finds the best fitting W-weights 
160: conditional on the regression based V-matrix. This procedure is fast and
161: often yields satisfactory results in terms of minimizing the MSPE. 
162: Specifying {cmd:nested} will lead to better performance, however, at the expense of additional computing time. 
163: If {cmd:nested} is specified
164: {cmd:synth} embarks on an fully nested optimization procedure
165:  that searches among all (diagonal) positive semidefinite V-matrices
166: and sets of W-weights for the best fitting convex combination of the control units.
167: The fully nested optimization 
168: contains the regression based V as a starting point, but often produces convex combinations that
169: achieve even lower MSPE. If {cmd: customV} is specified and {cmd: nested} is specified,
170: the user supplied V-matrix form the starting point for the nested optimization. 
171: All parameters of both optimizers can be tuned by the user depending on
172: his application (see  {help synth##info:{it:optimset}}).
173: 
174: {p 4 8 2}
175: {cmd: allopt} if nested is specified (see {cmd:nested}) the user can also 
176: specify {cmd: allopt} if she is willing to trade-off even more computing time 
177: in order to gain fully robust results. Sometimes the search space may 
178: contain local minima such that the nested optimization procedure starting from the
179: regression based V-matrix may not find the global minimum in the parameter space.
180: {cmd: allopt} provides 
181: a robustness check by running the nested optimization three times using three 
182: different starting points (the regression based V, equal V-weights, and a third 
183: procedure that uses Stata's {help ml search} procedure to find good starting values.
184: {cmd: synth} returns the best result of all three attempts. This option
185: usually will take three times the amount of computing time compared to the {cmd: nested} option.
186: Often {cmd: allopt}
187: will lead to no improvement over just the {cmd: nested} method, but sometime {cmd: allopt} produces even better results.

546: /* Set up quadratic programming */

548:  mat `c' = (-1 * ((`Xtr')' * `V' * `Xco'))'
549:  mat `A' = J(1,rowsof(`c'),1)

1: /* subroutine lossfunction: loss function for nested optimization */
2: program synth_ll
3:         version 9.2
4:         args todo b lnf
5:         tempname loss loss_final loss_var bb VV H c A l u wsol
6:         *matrix list `b'
7: 
8:        /* get abs constrained weights and create V */
9:         mata: getabs("`b'")
10:         mat `bb' = matout
11:         mat `VV' = diag(`bb')
12: 
13:        /* Set up quadratic programming */
14:         mat `H' =  ($Xco)' * `VV' * $Xco
15:         mat `c' = (-1 * (($Xtr)' * `VV' * $Xco))'
16:         mat `A' = J(1,rowsof(`c'),1)
17:         mat `l' = J(rowsof(`c'),1,0)
18:         mat `u' = J(rowsof(`c'),1,1)
19: 
20:       /* Initialize read out matrix  */
21:       matrix `wsol' = `l'
22: 
23:      /* do quadratic programming step  */
24:       plugin call synthopt , `c' `H'  `A' $bslack `l' `u' $bd $marg $maxit $sig `wsol'
25: 
26:      /* Compute loss */
27:       mat `loss' = ($Ztr - $Zco * `wsol')' * ( $Ztr - $Zco * `wsol')
28:       qui svmat  double `loss' ,names(`loss_var')
29:       qui gen    double `loss_final' = -1 * `loss_var'
30:       qui mlsum  `lnf'  = `loss_final' if `loss_var' ~=.
31: *      sum    `loss_final'
32:       qui drop   `loss_final' `loss_var'
33: end /* main program ends finally */
34: 
35: /* subroutine quadratic programming (C++ plugin) */
36: program synthopt, plugin

1: # Synth for Stata 0.0.8
2: 
3: ## Apple Silicon support
4: 
5: * **`synthopt.mac` is now a universal binary with arm64 + x86_64 slices.**
6:   Previously the binary covered `i386 / x86_64 / ppc_7400 / ppc64`, so
7:   Stata 17+ running natively on Apple Silicon failed to load the
8:   optimizer plugin with `Could not load plugin: synthopt.plugin`. The
9:   plugin is now built fresh from `plugin-src/` for both architectures.
10: * `synth.pkg` adds a `MACAPPLESIL` mapping so the SSC installer copies
11:   the correct binary on M-series Macs.
12: 
13: ## C portability fixes (in `plugin-src/`)
14: 
15: These three issues prevented the plugin from compiling on macOS or
16: Linux without manual edits:
17: 
18: * `synthopt.c`: `#include <malloc.h>` -> `#include <stdlib.h>`.
19:   `<malloc.h>` is not portable; `malloc`/`calloc`/`free` live in
20:   `<stdlib.h>` per ISO C.
21: * `synthopt.c`: `sprintf_s` -> `snprintf` shim. The Microsoft Annex K
22:   function is now wrapped with a portable macro on non-MSVC compilers.
23: * `pr_loqo.c`: explicit `min`/`max` macros added at the top of the
24:   file. Previously the code relied on the compile environment to
25:   inject them, which fails on macOS/Linux.
26: 
27: ## Quality-of-life
28: 
29: * `synth.ado`: `version` declaration bumped from 9.2 (Stata 9, 2007) to
30:   13.0 (Stata 13, 2013). All Stata releases since 2013 support v13
31:   syntax; this stops Stata from interpreting the code under a 17-year-
32:   old compatibility layer.
33: * Numerous typo fixes in comments and a couple of error/output messages
34:   ("speperate"/"separate", "paranthesis"/"parenthesis", "wheter"/
35:   "whether", "varibale"/"variable", "aynthing"/"anything",
36:   "leat one predictor is pecified"/"least one predictor is specified",
37:   "accoringly"/"accordingly", "disentagngle"/"disentangle",
38:   "articifical"/"artificial", "liklihood"/"likelihood").
39: * Bumped `synth.ado` `*!version` header from 0.0.7 (Jan 2014) to 0.0.8.
40: 
41: ## Verified
42: 
43: The canonical smoking example (Abadie, Diamond, Hainmueller 2010 JASA)
44: reproduces byte-for-byte against the 0.0-7 baseline:
45: 
46: * `e(RMSPE)` = 1.9432331649 (unchanged)
47: * `e(V_matrix)`, `e(W_weights)`, `e(X_balance)`: all identical to 10
48:   decimal places.
49: 
50: See `dev/01_capture_baseline.do` and `dev/02_regression_check.do` for
51: the test harness.

1: *! Integration tests for synth — broader coverage than baseline.
2: *!
3: *! Exercises the main option paths so a refactor that breaks one of them
4: *! is caught even if the basic smoking baseline still reproduces:
5: *!
6: *!   t1: smoking, default (regression-based V)         — same as baseline
7: *!   t2: smoking, customV (bypass V optimization)
8: *!   t3: smoking, nested + xperiod
9: *!   t4: smoking, keep() saves a results dataset
10: *!   t5: germany, default (West Germany reunification, AJPS 2014)
11: *!
12: *! How to run from repo root:
13: *!   /Applications/Stata/StataMP.app/Contents/MacOS/stata-mp -b do dev/03_integration_tests.do
14: *!
15: *! Outputs:
16: *!   dev/integration_outputs.txt   key matrices for each test
17: *!   dev/integration_tests.log     full Stata log
18: 
19: clear all
20: set more off
21: set seed 20260429
22: 
23: adopath ++ "`c(pwd)'"
24: 
25: log using "dev/integration_tests.log", replace text
26: 
27: file open out using "dev/integration_outputs.txt", write replace text
28: file write out "Synth Stata integration tests — current source" _n _n
29: 
30: capture program drop dump_results
31: program dump_results
32:   args label
33:   file write out "==== `label' ====" _n
34:   file write out "RMSPE:" _n
35:   mat L = e(RMSPE)
36:   forv i = 1/`=rowsof(L)' {
37:     file write out %18.8f (L[`i',1]) _n
38:   }
39:   file write out "max V diag (proxy for V):" _n
40:   mat V = e(V_matrix)
41:   scalar mxV = .
42:   forv i = 1/`=rowsof(V)' {
43:     if (V[`i',`i'] > mxV | mxV >= .) scalar mxV = V[`i',`i']
44:   }
45:   file write out %18.8f (mxV) _n
46:   file write out "sum W weights:" _n
47:   mat W = e(W_weights)
48:   scalar sw = 0
49:   forv i = 1/`=rowsof(W)' {
50:     scalar sw = sw + W[`i',2]
51:   }
52:   file write out %18.8f (sw) _n _n
53: end
54:

56: display _newline as txt "=== t1: smoking default ==="
57: use "smoking.dta", clear
58: tsset state year
59: synth cigsale beer(1984(1)1988) lnincome retprice age15to24 cigsale(1988) ///
60:         cigsale(1980) cigsale(1975), trunit(3) trperiod(1989)
61: dump_results "t1 smoking default"

65: use "smoking.dta", clear
66: tsset state year

68:         cigsale(1980) cigsale(1975), trunit(3) trperiod(1989) ///
69:         customV(1 1 1 1 1 1 1)
70: dump_results "t2 smoking customV"

72: * -------------------- t3: smoking nested + xperiod --------------------
73: display _newline as txt "=== t3: smoking nested + xperiod ==="
74: use "smoking.dta", clear
75: tsset state year
76: synth cigsale beer lnincome retprice age15to24 cigsale(1988) cigsale(1980) cigsale(1975), ///
77:         trunit(3) trperiod(1989) xperiod(1980(1)1988) nested
78: dump_results "t3 smoking nested xperiod"

80: * -------------------- t4: smoking keep() --------------------
81: display _newline as txt "=== t4: smoking keep() ==="
82: use "smoking.dta", clear
83: tsset state year
84: tempfile saved_synth
85: synth cigsale beer(1984(1)1988) lnincome retprice age15to24 cigsale(1988) ///
86:         cigsale(1980) cigsale(1975), trunit(3) trperiod(1989) ///
87:         keep("`saved_synth'") replace
88: dump_results "t4 smoking keep"
89: * sanity check the saved file exists and has expected vars
90: preserve
91: use "`saved_synth'", clear
92: file write out "t4 saved-file vars: " _n
93: foreach v of varlist _all {
94:   file write out "  `v'" _n
95: }
96: file write out _n
97: restore

104:         schooling(1980&1985) invrate(1980&1985) gdppc(1960) gdppc(1970) gdppc(1980), ///
